key_insight: OmniQEC uses an LLM-driven slow–fast search loop to discover quantum error-correcting codes that are not only structurally promising, but also effective after syndrome-extraction and decoder-level evaluation.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets deployable QEC on real hardware by co-designing the code, circuit, and decoder under physical-qubit budgets, making it relevant for near-term fault-tolerant quantum engineering.
method: LLM orchestrator generates and iteratively refines QEC candidates
Fast loop screens codes with inexpensive code-level proxies
Slow loop evaluates full syndrome-extraction and decoding circuits, then feeds results back into search
evidence_signal: Across four qLDPC families and three LLM backends, the discovered codes improved logical-error suppression with larger physical-qubit budgets and outperformed BB codes at complete-implementation budgets of 98 and 240 physical qubits.
watch_item: Results depend on the chosen hardware model, syndrome-extraction design, and decoder quality, so practical gains may not transfer uniformly across processors or implementation constraints.
paper_title: OmniQEC: discovering practical quantum error-correcting codes by an AI scientist
